hook.line: Part two of how to categorize your videos to escape the 200-300 view jail.
hook.visual: Sunlit handheld selfie close-up; white title 'How to Auto Generate a Description Box' at top and a reply-to-comment sticker under it.

beats.what: Part-two framing and the 'view jail' pain, with the title and the viewer's comment sticker already on screen.
Small text note: the description box is part 2 of categorizing, do all 5 steps.
The rule: always pick the 10-minute recording option, never 15 s/30 s/60 s.
Worked example: a 28 s video, keep recording until it passes 61 s.
First cut: this guarantees TikTok auto-generates the description box.
Cut: then trim the clip back down to the part where you actually talk.
Cut: one-breath recap of the three rules.
Text note reminds viewers to still do the 5 steps from the prior video.
Asks supporters to send a gift, then for questions in the comments.

why_it_works: Reply-to-comment format: the viewer's question is pinned on screen, so it feels like a personal answer and proves demand.
Names a pain everyone small fears ('view jail') and promises a 'guaranteed' fix, which raises stakes for a tiny technical trick.
One specific, checkable hack (record past 61 s, then trim) that people can test right away, which drives comments (3.8k) and shares (5.3k).
A persistent title at the top keeps the topic readable for anyone who joins mid-video.
weaknesses: Almost no visual change: 3 cuts in 72 s and the first only at 33 s; the face fills the frame in harsh sunlight.
No captions for the spoken steps and no screen recording of where the description box actually appears.
The rules are repeated several times, padding the video past a minute.
Ends on a gift request, which is a weak payoff for the viewer.
for_robert: Steal the reply-to-comment sticker plus persistent title, but avoid the static minute: when he says 'it'll be right here', cut to the screen and let Fred point at the spot.
